script: In 1953, a young lawyer named Fidel Castro led over a hundred rebels in a surprise attack, and it failed completely. Their target was the Moncada Barracks, the second largest military fortress in all of Cuba, defended by hundreds of soldiers. The plan fell apart within minutes, as their cars got lost in the unfamiliar city and the rebels lost the element of surprise. Dozens of Castro's men were captured, brutally tortured, and then executed by the furious soldiers of the dictator Batista. Castro himself was caught days later hiding in the mountains, and dragged into a courtroom to be silenced for good. But here is the twist that nobody in power expected: he turned his own trial into a weapon against them. He delivered a two hour speech that ended with four unforgettable words, history will absolve me. Sentenced to fifteen years, he was quietly freed in under two, and slipped away to Mexico to rebuild his army. Six years after his humiliating defeat, Fidel Castro marched into Havana and seized control of the entire country. And to this very day, Cuba's revolution is named the twenty sixth of July, after the exact battle that he lost.

title: How Fidel Castro's Worst Defeat Became Cuba's Revolution
description:
July 26, 1953: Fidel Castro led over a hundred rebels against the Moncada Barracks. The attack was a catastrophe. Most were captured, tortured, or killed, and Castro was put on trial. He turned it into his famous 'History Will Absolve Me' speech, walked free in two years, and six years later seized Cuba. The revolution named itself after the date of that defeat.
